raw_response:
I’m an older man and I’ve farmed this land long enough that I don’t like to gamble much. With only 19.1 mu and just myself in the household, I have to keep the work manageable and not spend too much cash at once. Wheat and maize is still the safest way for me. Everybody around here does it, and I know this rotation well. I have a well, so for wheat I will not be too stingy with water, because if the wheat misses water at the key stage, the yield drops hard. Fertilizer, I still do about the same as usual, maybe a little careful on the high side for wheat because wheat responds well and I hate seeing a pale field. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I won’t do fancy tillage. I’ll harvest wheat, clear the field quickly, and get maize in right away. Since I’m middle-school educated, I do pay attention to what the extension people say, but in the end I still adjust by what my own field did last year. I want a steady harvest more than chasing the very highest yield.
